grammar.title: 对 as a preposition
grammar.pattern: A + 对 + B + Verb/Adjective；对 + sb + 来说，…
grammar.explain: As a preposition, 对 means 'to' or 'towards' and introduces the person or thing an attitude or action is directed at. It comes before the verb or adjective: 对学生很好 'good to the students'. 对…来说 means 'for (someone)' or 'as far as (someone) is concerned'.

examples.zh: 对 我 来 说 ， 这 是 一 次 很 好 的 机会 。

grammar.title: 当…的时候 'when…'
grammar.pattern: 当 + clause + 的时候，…
grammar.explain: 当…的时候 means 'when' or 'at the time when'. 当 opens the time clause and 的时候 closes it. In speech 当 is often dropped, but keeping it sounds a little more formal and clear.

grammar.title: 却 'but, yet'
grammar.pattern: Subject + 却 + Verb/Adjective
grammar.explain: 却 shows that something is contrary to what you would expect. Unlike 但是, which starts a clause, 却 is an adverb: it goes after the subject and before the verb. 但是 and 却 can be used together: 但是他却….

reading.title: 我在北京的新生活
reading.zh: 去年秋天，我离开家，来到北京工作。刚来的时候，所有的事情对我来说都很新鲜，不过也有不少困难。当我第一次一个人坐地铁的时候，我不知道应该在哪儿换车，最后在一位阿姨的帮助下才找到了公司。那时候我常常感觉很孤单，晚上回到家，房间里安静得让人难过。妈妈常常打电话来问我的情况，让我一定要注意安全。我没有放弃，而是继续努力工作，周末去参加各种活动，认识了很多新朋友。现在，我已经通过了公司的考试，成为了正式员工。我的生活发生了很大的变化，一切都越来越好。虽然北京的冬天冷死了，我却越来越喜欢这座城市。对我来说，这里已经成为了我的第二个家。
reading.en: Last autumn I left home and came to Beijing to work. When I first arrived, everything was new to me, but there were also quite a few difficulties. The first time I took the subway on my own, I didn't know where to change lines, and in the end I only found my company with the help of an older lady. Back then I often felt lonely; when I got home at night, my room was so quiet it made me sad. My mom often called to ask how I was doing and told me to be careful. I didn't give up. Instead, I kept working hard, joined all kinds of activities on weekends and made lots of new friends. Now I've passed the company's exam and become a permanent employee. My life has changed a lot, and everything keeps getting better. Although winter in Beijing is freezing, I like this city more and more. For me, it has already become my second home.

grammar.title: 只要…就… 'as long as'
grammar.pattern: 只要 + condition，(Subject +) 就 + result
grammar.explain: 只要 introduces a condition that is enough to bring about a result, and 就 introduces that result. It means 'as long as' or 'provided that'. If the second clause has a subject, it comes before 就.

examples.zh: 只要 你 努力 ， 就 一定 能 成功 。

examples.zh: 只要 有 时间 ， 我 就 去 锻炼 。

grammar.title: 连…也/都… 'even'
grammar.pattern: 连 + emphasized element + 也/都 + Verb
grammar.explain: 连 marks something surprising or extreme, like English 'even'. The emphasized word goes right after 连, and 也 or 都 comes before the verb. It is very common in negative sentences.

examples.zh: 这 个 问题 太 简单 了 ， 连 孩子 都 会 。

examples.zh: 他 连 我 的 名字 都 忘记 了 。

grammar.title: 甚至 'even; to the point that'
grammar.pattern: …，(Subject +) 甚至 + Verb…
grammar.explain: 甚至 introduces the most extreme example in a series, like 'even' or 'so much so that'. It usually starts the last clause or goes before the verb, and is often combined with 连…都/也.

reading.title: 一次调查
reading.zh: 上个月，我们公司计划组织一次周末旅游。为了了解大家的想法，经理让我做一个调查。我给每个同事都发了一份调查表，一共有四十个人回答了，其中三十个人支持这个计划，可是也有一部分人不想去。我问他们原因，有的人说周末要陪孩子，有的人甚至说连周末都要加班，实在没有时间。当时我觉得这个计划可能不会成功。后来我改变了方法：活动不在周末，而改在星期五下午，并且大家可以带家人一起来。结果，几乎所有的人都接受了这个新计划。经理听到这个消息以后非常高兴，他说：“只要方法对，问题就能解决。看来你真正有组织能力！”
reading.en: Last month our company planned a weekend trip. To find out what everyone thought, the manager asked me to do a survey. I sent a questionnaire to every colleague. Forty people replied in total; thirty of them supported the plan, but some didn't want to go. When I asked them why, some said they had to look after their children on weekends, and some even said they had to work overtime even on weekends and really had no time. At the time I thought the plan might fail. Then I changed my approach: the trip would not be on the weekend but on Friday afternoon instead, and everyone could bring their family along. As a result, almost everyone accepted the new plan. When the manager heard the news, he was delighted. He said, 'As long as the method is right, problems can be solved. It looks like you really have a talent for organizing!'

grammar.title: 因此 'therefore'
grammar.pattern: Cause，因此 + Result
grammar.explain: 因此 means 'therefore' or 'as a result'. It begins the clause that gives the result. It is a little more formal than 所以 and is often paired with 由于 rather than 因为.

examples.zh: 他 一直 坚持 锻炼 ， 因此 身体 很 健康 。

grammar.title: 好像 'seem; as if'
grammar.pattern: Subject + 好像 + Verb/Adjective；好像…一样
grammar.explain: 好像 means 'seem' or 'look like' and goes before the verb or adjective. It softens a statement when you aren't completely sure. 好像…一样 means 'just like' or 'as if'.

examples.zh: 他 高兴 得 好像 一 个 孩子 一样 。

grammar.title: 到底 in questions
grammar.pattern: Subject + 到底 + Verb / question word…？
grammar.explain: In questions, 到底 adds the feeling of 'exactly' or 'on earth', showing that the speaker really wants a clear answer. It goes before the verb or the question word. It is not used in questions ending in 吗.

reading.title: 第一次献血
reading.zh: 上个星期六，我第一次参加了学校组织的献血活动。说实话，我一开始挺害怕的，因为我从来没献过血。医生先给我做了检查，告诉我一切正常，另外还提醒我前一天晚上要好好休息。献血的时候，我好像一点儿也没觉得疼，十分钟左右就结束了。护士说，我的血也许能帮助一个病人留住生命。听了这句话，我心里特别激动。活动结束以后，学校还给每位同学提供了一份小礼物，校长代表病人和他们的家人感谢我们。这次经历让我明白：帮助别人不只是一个任务，更是一种精神。因此，我决定以后每年都坚持献血。
reading.en: Last Saturday I took part in a blood drive organized by my school for the first time. To be honest, I was quite scared at first, because I had never given blood before. The doctor examined me first and told me everything was normal; she also reminded me to rest well the night before. While I was giving blood, I didn't seem to feel any pain at all, and it was over in about ten minutes. The nurse said my blood might help save a patient's life. When I heard that, I was really moved. After the event, the school gave every student a small gift, and the headmaster thanked us on behalf of the patients and their families. This experience made me understand that helping others is not just a task — it's a kind of spirit. So I've decided to keep giving blood every year from now on.

grammar.title: 不管…都… 'no matter'
grammar.pattern: 不管 + question word / A还是B / 多 + Adj，Subject + 都/也 + Verb
grammar.explain: 不管 means 'no matter' or 'regardless of'. The first clause must contain a question word (什么, 谁, 怎么, 多…), an 'A 还是 B' choice or a 'verb-not-verb' form. The second clause uses 都 or 也 to show that the result stays the same. 不管 is a little more colloquial than 无论.

examples.zh: 不管 天气 怎么样 ， 他 都 去 公园 跑步 。
examples.en: Whatever the weather, he goes running in the park.

examples.zh: 不管 多 忙 ， 父亲 都 会 给 我 打电话 。

grammar.title: 首先…然后…最后 'first…then…finally'
grammar.pattern: 首先…，然后…，最后…
grammar.explain: 首先 means 'first (of all)'. Use it with 然后 ('then') and 最后 ('finally') to list steps in order. 首先 can also introduce the most important point in an argument.

examples.zh: 首先 我们 要 了解 情况 ， 然后 再 做 决定 。
examples.en: First we need to understand the situation; then we'll make a decision.

examples.zh: 首先 认真 读 题 ， 然后 再 写 答案 。

grammar.title: 原来 'originally' and 'so it turns out'
grammar.pattern: Subject + 原来 + Verb…，后来…；原来 + clause！
grammar.explain: 原来 has two common uses. It can mean 'originally' or 'formerly', contrasting the past with the present. It also expresses a sudden discovery: 'so that's it' or 'it turns out'. In the second use it usually starts the sentence.

reading.title: 我的父亲
reading.zh: 我的父亲是一名记者，已经工作了二十多年。小时候，我常常不理解他：为什么他总是那么忙？不管是周末还是节日，只要有新闻，他都会马上出发。有一次，城里一座老楼着火了，情况非常严重。父亲是第一个到那里的记者。他首先了解了发生了什么，然后跟附近的人谈话，最后他一晚上没睡觉，写出了一篇报道。这篇报道受到了很多人的注意，大家开始讨论老房子的安全问题。后来，楼里的人都被重新安排了住的地方。父亲告诉我，记者的责任就是让大家知道真实的情况。原来，他的工作确实很重要！现在我也上了大学，选择了新闻专业。我的梦是像父亲一样，用自己的文章让社会变得更好。
reading.en: My father is a journalist and has been working for more than twenty years. When I was little, I often didn't understand him: why was he always so busy? Whether it was a weekend or a holiday, as soon as there was news, he would set off right away. Once, an old building in the city caught fire, and the situation was very serious. My father was the first journalist to get there. First he found out what had happened, then he talked with people nearby, and finally he stayed up all night writing a report. The report got a lot of attention, and people began to discuss the safety of old buildings. Later, everyone in the building was given a new place to live. My father told me that a journalist's responsibility is to let everyone know the true situation. So his job really was important! Now I'm at university too, and I've chosen journalism as my major. My dream is to be like my father and use my writing to make society better.

units.goal: Talk about stress and setbacks, and say you'll keep going even when things are hard.

grammar.title: 即使…也… 'even if'
grammar.pattern: 即使 + condition，Subject + 也 + Verb
grammar.explain: 即使 means 'even if'. It introduces a condition, often a hypothetical or extreme one, and 也 in the second clause shows that the result stays the same. It is common in both speech and writing.

examples.zh: 即使 明天 下雨 ， 比赛 也 会 继续 进行 。
examples.en: Even if it rains tomorrow, the match will go ahead.

examples.zh: 即使 很 累 ， 她 也 不 想 放弃 。

grammar.title: 尽管…可是/仍然… 'although'
grammar.pattern: 尽管 + fact，(可是/但是) Subject + 仍然/还是 + Verb
grammar.explain: 尽管 means 'although' or 'despite the fact that'. Unlike 即使, the first clause states a real fact, not a supposition. The second clause often begins with 可是 or 但是 and uses 仍然 or 还是 ('still').

examples.zh: 尽管 天气 很 冷 ， 可是 大家 都 玩 得 很 高兴 。

grammar.title: 由于 'due to'
grammar.pattern: 由于 + reason，(因此/所以) + result
grammar.explain: 由于 means 'due to' or 'because of'. It is more formal than 因为 and is common in news, notices and written Chinese. It can be followed by a noun phrase or a whole clause.

reading.title: 一次比赛
reading.zh: 去年，我报名参加了学校的汉语比赛，要在台上用汉语讲五分钟。比赛前一个月，我每天都在准备，压力特别大。由于太紧张，我有好几次都想放弃。母亲看出了我的心情，对我说：“即使不能赢，这也是一次值得的经历。最重要的不是结果，而是准备的过程。”听了她的话，我觉得轻松了许多。后来，我请老师和同学给我提意见，大家一起讨论怎么把我的话讲得更自然。比赛那天，台下坐满了人。尽管我紧张得一直出汗，我仍然顺利地讲完了。最后，我得了第二名。这次经历说明，无论做什么，只要不放弃，就会有好的结果。
reading.en: Last year I signed up for my school's Chinese competition, where I had to speak in Chinese on stage for five minutes. For a month before the competition I prepared every day, and the pressure was enormous. Because I was so nervous, I wanted to give up several times. My mother noticed how I felt and said to me, 'Even if you don't win, it'll be an experience worth having. What matters most isn't the result but the process of preparing.' After hearing that, I felt much more relaxed. Later I asked my teacher and classmates for suggestions, and we discussed together how to make what I said sound more natural. On the day of the competition, the hall was full. Although I was so nervous that I kept sweating, I still got through my speech smoothly. In the end, I came second. This experience shows that whatever you do, as long as you don't give up, you'll get a good result.

grammar.title: Rhetorical questions with 难道…吗
grammar.pattern: 难道 + Subject + Verb… + 吗？
grammar.explain: 难道…吗 forms a rhetorical question that shows surprise, disbelief or a strong opinion, like 'Don't tell me…' or 'Surely you don't…?'. The speaker isn't really asking: a positive 难道 question implies 'no', and a negative one implies 'yes'. 难道 can go before or after the subject.

grammar.title: 于是 'so; and then'
grammar.pattern: Event 1，于是 (+ Subject) + Event 2
grammar.explain: 于是 links two past events: the second happens as a result of the first, like 'so' or 'and so'. It is used in narration, not for advice or commands. It usually starts the second clause.

examples.zh: 他 觉得 这 个 专业 很 适合 自己 ， 于是 就 选择 了 它 。

grammar.title: 从来 + 不/没 'never'
grammar.pattern: Subject + 从来 + 不 + Verb；Subject + 从来 + 没(有) + Verb + 过

reading.title: 选专业
reading.zh: 上大学以前，我遇到了一个很大的困难：选什么专业？我本来对艺术很有兴趣，想学画画，可是父母觉得这个专业不好找工作。他们希望我学管理或者经济，因为市场上需要这方面的人，工作条件也比较好。我们为这件事吵了好几次。后来，我的老师对我说：“选专业最关键的是找到适合自己的方向。难道你愿意每天做自己不喜欢的事情吗？”于是，我决定跟父母好好谈一谈。我告诉他们，我从来没有这么认真地考虑过一件事。最后，他们同意了。现在我已经正式成为艺术专业的学生，虽然学习很辛苦，但是我十分快乐。
reading.en: Before going to university, I faced a big difficulty: which major should I choose? I had always been interested in art and wanted to study painting, but my parents thought it would be hard to find a job with that major. They hoped I would study management or economics, because the job market needs people in those fields and the working conditions are better. We argued about it several times. Later, my teacher said to me, 'The key to choosing a major is finding the direction that suits you. Do you really want to spend every day doing things you don't like?' So I decided to have a proper talk with my parents. I told them I had never thought about anything so seriously. In the end, they agreed. Now I'm officially an art student. Although studying is hard work, I'm extremely happy.

reading.zh: 我的朋友小林大学毕业以后成了一名律师。这是一份很多人羡慕的职业：收入高，工作环境也不错。可是工作了五年以后，他发现自己每天早上醒来心情都很差。他真正喜欢的是电影。于是，他决定放弃律师工作，去学拍电影。他的父母和朋友几乎都反对，觉得他的想法太奇怪了。小林却说：“生命只有一次，我不想后悔。”为了省钱，他租了一个很小的房间，每天学习到很晚。三年以后，他拍出了自己的第一个电影。电影讲的是一家人的感情故事，内容很简单，效果却特别好，观众都说非常精彩。让大家没想到的是，这个电影竟然在一个国际电影节上得了奖！现在小林常说：“以前的律师经验让我更懂得怎么讲故事。”
reading.en: After graduating from university, my friend Xiao Lin became a lawyer. It's a profession many people envy: the income is high and the working environment is good. But after five years, he found that he woke up in a bad mood every morning. What he really loved was film. So he decided to give up his job as a lawyer and learn filmmaking. Almost all his parents and friends were against it; they thought his idea was too strange. But Xiao Lin said, 'You only live once, and I don't want to have regrets.' To save money, he rented a tiny room and studied until late every night. Three years later, he made his first film. It told the emotional story of a family. The content was simple, but it worked brilliantly, and audiences all said it was wonderful. To everyone's surprise, the film actually won a prize at an international film festival! Now Xiao Lin often says, 'My experience as a lawyer taught me how to tell a story better.'

grammar.title: 不仅…而且… 'not only…but also'

grammar.explain: 不仅 ('not only') introduces a first point, and 而且 (or 也/还) adds a further, often stronger, point. If both clauses have the same subject, put the subject before 不仅. 不仅 is a little more formal than 不但.

reading.title: 一场免费的演出
reading.zh: 上个月，一个著名的艺术团来我们城市演出，而且是免费的！消息一发出来，很多人都想去看。不过，想看演出要先在网上申请，因为座位不多，竞争非常大。我和妻子一起申请，没想到我们俩竟然都成功了。演出那天晚上，里面坐满了观众。演员的动作又漂亮又整齐，音乐也十分好听，深深地吸引了每一个人。演出中间，演员还请几个当地的孩子上台一起表演，大家都笑了。我估计这场演出大概有两个小时，可是我一点儿也不觉得长。回家的路上，妻子说：“这样的演出不仅让人快乐，而且让我们更了解了艺术。以后有机会，咱们还要来。”
reading.en: Last month a famous performing arts group came to our city to perform — and it was free! As soon as the news came out, lots of people wanted to go. But to see the show you had to apply online first, and since there weren't many seats, the competition was fierce. My wife and I both applied, and to our surprise we both got in. On the night of the show, the hall was packed. The performers' movements were beautiful and perfectly in sync, and the music was lovely too; it completely captivated everyone. In the middle of the show, the performers invited a few local children on stage to perform with them, and everyone laughed. I reckon the show lasted about two hours, but it didn't feel long at all. On the way home my wife said, 'A show like this doesn't just make people happy — it also helps us understand art better. Let's come again when we get the chance.'

reading.zh: 大学毕业以后，我和三个同学决定一起去南方旅行。我们共同的爱好是爬山和吃好吃的东西。既然大家都有时间，我们就开始做计划。首先要考虑的是交通：坐飞机快，但是价格太贵；坐火车便宜，距离也不算太远，于是我们选择了坐火车。出发前一天，小王在杂志上看了一篇文章，提醒大家：“那边的天气很复杂，最好带上伞。另外，钱包和护照千万别丢了！”到了那里，我们发现周围的风景比照片上还美，当地的菜味道也特别好。一个星期很快就过去了，大家玩得非常轻松。回来的时候，我们都说：毕业了，友谊不能断，以后每年都要一起出去旅行。
reading.en: After graduating from university, three classmates and I decided to travel to the south together. Our shared interests are hiking and eating good food. Since we all had time, we started making plans. The first thing to consider was transport: flying is fast, but it's too expensive; the train is cheap and the distance isn't too far, so we chose the train. The day before we set off, Xiao Wang read an article in a magazine and reminded everyone, 'The weather there is unpredictable, so we'd better take umbrellas. Also, whatever you do, don't lose your wallets and passports!' When we got there, we found the scenery around us was even more beautiful than in the photos, and the local food tasted wonderful. The week flew by, and we all had a really relaxing time. On the way back, we all agreed: now that we've graduated, our friendship mustn't fade, and we'll travel together every year.

grammar.title: 究竟 'exactly; on earth'
grammar.pattern: Subject + 究竟 + question…？
grammar.explain: 究竟 works like 到底: in questions it means 'exactly' or 'on earth', pushing for the real answer. It is a little more formal than 到底 and common in writing. Like 到底, it is not used in questions ending in 吗.

grammar.title: Degree complements: 得很 / 得厉害
grammar.pattern: Verb/Adjective + 得 + 很/厉害；Verb/Adjective + 得 + result

reading.title: 网上的生活
reading.zh: 现在，上网已经成为我们生活中很重要的一部分。我们在网站上看新闻、读文章，用手机跟世界上不同国家的人交流。然而，网上的东西不一定都是真的。上个月，我奶奶就差点被人骗了。她收到一条消息，说她的孙子出了事，需要马上给对方转一万块钱。奶奶激动得不得了，差点就转了钱。还好她先给我打了个电话，我告诉她这是骗人的。其实，不管年龄大还是小，都有可能被骗。在网上我们不能随便信任别人，遇到要钱的事情，一定要先问清楚，看看究竟是怎么回事。另外，上网虽然方便，但也不要浪费太多时间。有的人躺在床上玩一晚上手机，第二天困得厉害，实在可惜。
reading.en: These days, the internet has become a very important part of our lives. We read news and articles on websites and use our phones to communicate with people from different countries around the world. However, not everything online is true. Last month my grandma was almost scammed. She received a message saying her grandson was in trouble and that she needed to transfer ten thousand yuan right away. Grandma got terribly worked up and nearly sent the money. Luckily she called me first, and I told her it was a scam. In fact, whether you're old or young, you could be cheated. Online, we can't trust people casually. When someone asks for money, we must ask clear questions first and find out what's really going on. Also, although the internet is convenient, don't waste too much time on it. Some people lie in bed playing on their phones all night and are terribly sleepy the next day, which is a real shame.

grammar.title: 恐怕 'I'm afraid; probably'
grammar.pattern: 恐怕 + clause；Subject + 恐怕 + Verb
grammar.explain: 恐怕 means 'I'm afraid (that)' or 'probably'. It makes a worried or polite guess, usually about something unwelcome. It can go before or after the subject.

grammar.title: Potential complements: Verb + 得/不 + result
grammar.pattern: Verb + 得 + complement (can)；Verb + 不 + complement (can't)
grammar.explain: Put 得 between a verb and its result or direction complement to say something can be done, or 不 to say it can't: 听得懂 'can understand (by listening)', 吃不完 'can't finish eating'. Verb + 得了/不了 means 'can/can't manage'. These forms are more natural than 能/不能 for whether a result can be achieved.

reading.title: 我和北京
reading.zh: 三个月前，我从南方搬到了北京。我出生在一个小城市，那里一年四季都很暖和，到处都是绿色。刚来北京的时候，我很不适应：冬天特别冷，空气也很干燥，我的皮肤总是不舒服。另外，我对周围的环境完全不熟悉，常常走错路，有一次还在地铁站里撞到了别人。工作上，我暂时还没交到朋友，同事们好像都很忙。说实话，我对北京的第一印象不太好，甚至有点儿失望。不过，慢慢地，我发现这座城市也有很多可爱的地方。冬天的阳光很美，北方的面条和汤也很好吃。同事们其实都很热情，常常互相帮助。现在我的收入比以前高，生活也越来越习惯了。恐怕再过一段时间，我就会真正爱上这里吧。
reading.en: Three months ago I moved from the south to Beijing. I was born in a small city where it's warm all year round and everything is green. When I first came to Beijing, I found it very hard to adjust: the winter is extremely cold, the air is very dry, and my skin always felt uncomfortable. Besides, I didn't know my surroundings at all and often got lost; once I even bumped into someone in a subway station. At work, I haven't made any friends yet, and my colleagues all seem very busy. To be honest, my first impression of Beijing wasn't good, and I was even a little disappointed. But gradually I've discovered that this city has lots of lovely things too. The winter sunshine is beautiful, and northern noodles and soups are delicious. My colleagues are actually very warm and often help one another. Now my income is higher than before, and I'm getting more and more used to life here. I suspect that before long, I'll truly fall in love with this place.

grammar.title: 尤其 'especially'
grammar.pattern: …，尤其(是) + Noun / 尤其 + Verb/Adjective
grammar.explain: 尤其 means 'especially' or 'particularly'. It singles out the member of a group that stands out most. It usually appears in the second part of a sentence, often as 尤其是 + noun, or right before an adjective or verb.

examples.zh: 我 喜欢 运动 ， 尤其 是 游泳 。

grammar.title: 把 with place, recipient and result complements
grammar.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + 在/到/给/成/掉…
grammar.explain: When an object is moved to a place, given to someone or got rid of, Chinese normally uses a 把 sentence: 把书放在桌子上, 把房子租给学生, 把旧报纸扔掉. The verb in a 把 sentence can't stand alone; it needs something after it, such as a complement or 了.

reading.title: 我的博士生活
reading.zh: 我叫小陈，正在读博士。我的老师是一位很严格的教授，他常说：“光有知识还不够，最重要的是学会判断问题。”每天早上，我骑自行车去学校，学校离我租的房子正好三公里。读博士很辛苦，工资也不高，每个月交完房租，就剩不下多少钱了。有时候工作不顺利，我会对自己没有信心，甚至想放弃。不过，读博士也有很多好处：我可以专门研究自己有兴趣的问题，还认识了很多有趣的朋友。尤其是我的同学安娜，她总是主动帮助别人，遇到困难也从来不着急。周末，我们常常一起去附近的公园散步，或者听她弹钢琴。我的看法是，不管做什么，只要喜欢，再苦也值得。
reading.en: My name is Xiao Chen, and I'm doing a PhD. My supervisor is a very strict professor. He often says, 'Knowledge alone isn't enough; the most important thing is learning to judge problems.' Every morning I cycle to school, which is exactly three kilometers from the place I rent. Doing a PhD is hard work and the pay isn't high; after paying the rent each month, there isn't much money left. Sometimes when work isn't going well, I lose confidence in myself and even want to give up. But doing a PhD also has many benefits: I can focus on researching questions I'm interested in, and I've met lots of interesting friends. Especially my classmate Anna — she always takes the initiative to help others and never panics when she runs into trouble. On weekends we often go for walks in the nearby park, or I listen to her play the piano. My view is that whatever you do, as long as you love it, it's worth it, however hard it is.

grammar.title: Passive sentences with 被/叫/让
grammar.pattern: Receiver + 被/叫/让 + (Agent) + Verb + complement/了
grammar.explain: In a passive sentence the receiver of the action comes first, and 被, 叫 or 让 introduces the doer. 叫 and 让 are colloquial and must be followed by the doer; with 被 the doer can be left out. The verb usually has a complement or 了, and passive sentences often describe something unwelcome.

grammar.explain: 一 + measure word + noun + 也/都 + negative stresses 'not even one'. 一点儿也不 + adjective means 'not at all'. The 一-phrase goes before the verb, not after it as in English.

reading.title: 楼下的小书店
reading.zh: 我家楼下有一家小书店，开书店的是一位五十多岁的阿姨。书店不大，里面的书却很丰富，从流行小说到历史书，什么都有。书店里有点儿暗，但是很安静，平时很多学生喜欢来这里看书。阿姨对每一位顾客都很热情，常常跟大家聊天，还会详细地介绍每本书的作者和内容。有一次，一个孩子不小心把一本新书弄坏了，他很害怕，以为会被批评。没想到阿姨不但原谅了他，还鼓励他以后多读书。这件小事让我很感动。上个月，书店举办了一次读书活动，请来了一位作者跟大家见面，那天书店里坐满了人。阿姨说，她的理想就是让更多的人爱上读书。我希望这家小书店能一直开下去。
reading.en: There's a little bookshop downstairs from my home, run by a woman in her fifties. The shop isn't big, but it has a rich selection of books — everything from popular novels to history books. It's a bit dark inside but very quiet, and lots of students usually like to come and read there. The owner is warm to every customer; she often chats with people and describes each book's author and content in detail. Once, a child accidentally damaged a new book. He was scared and thought he would be told off. To his surprise, she not only forgave him but also encouraged him to read more. This little incident really touched me. Last month the bookshop held a reading event and invited an author to meet everyone; the shop was packed that day. The owner says her dream is to get more people to fall in love with reading. I hope this little bookshop stays open for a long time.

grammar.title: 随着 'along with; as'
grammar.pattern: 随着 + Noun (的 + change)，Subject + 越来越/逐渐/也 + change
grammar.explain: 随着 means 'along with' or 'as (something changes)'. It introduces a change that brings about another change. It is usually followed by a noun phrase such as 经济的发展 or 年龄的增长, and the main clause often has 越来越, 逐渐 or 也.

examples.zh: 随着 经济 的 发展 ， 我们 的 生活 越来越 好 了 。
examples.en: As the economy develops, our lives keep getting better.

grammar.title: 果然 'sure enough'
grammar.pattern: Subject + 果然 + Verb/Adjective
grammar.explain: 果然 means 'sure enough' or 'just as expected'. It shows that something turned out exactly as someone predicted. Compare 竟然, which is used when something turns out against expectations.

examples.zh: 大家 都 说 这 个 菜 好吃 ， 果然 不 错 。

examples.zh: 我 猜 他 会 迟到 ， 他 果然 迟到 了 。

grammar.title: 只好 'have no choice but to'
grammar.pattern: Subject + 只好 + Verb
grammar.explain: 只好 means 'have to' or 'can only', because there is no better option. It is similar to 不得不 but sounds more resigned, and usually describes a decision already made. The subject, if there is one, comes before 只好.

reading.title: 生活的变化
reading.zh: 随着科学技术的发展，我们的生活发生了很大的变化。二十年前，购物要去商店，现在在手机上点一点，东西第二天就送到家了。以前出门一定要带钥匙和钱包，现在很多人家里用的是密码门，买东西也用手机。不过，变化也带来了问题。城市里的车越来越多，空气污染越来越严重，森林逐渐减少，地球的温度也越来越高。有人说，如果我们不改变自己的习惯，将来的情况会更不好。去年夏天特别热，我想买一台空调，跑了好几家商店，空调果然都卖完了，我只好每天开着窗户睡觉。我想，为了降低污染，每个人都应该勇敢地做出改变：少用塑料袋，多坐公共汽车，多种树。
reading.en: With the development of science and technology, our lives have changed enormously. Twenty years ago, you had to go to a shop to buy things; now you tap a few times on your phone and your purchase arrives at your door the next day. In the past you always had to take your keys and wallet when you went out; now many homes have password locks, and people pay for things with their phones. But change has also brought problems. There are more and more cars in cities, air pollution is getting worse, forests are gradually shrinking, and the Earth is getting warmer. Some people say that if we don't change our habits, things will be even worse in the future. Last summer was extremely hot. I wanted to buy an air conditioner and went to several shops, but sure enough, they were all sold out, so I had to sleep with the windows open every night. I think that to reduce pollution, everyone should bravely make changes: use fewer plastic bags, take the bus more and plant more trees.

grammar.title: 例如 'for example'
grammar.pattern: General statement，例如 + A、B(等)
grammar.explain: 例如 means 'for example' or 'such as'. It introduces one or more examples after a general statement and is often followed by a list that ends in 等. It is slightly more formal than 比如.

grammar.title: 相反 'on the contrary; opposite'
grammar.pattern: A…，相反，B…；A 跟 B + 相反
grammar.explain: 相反 means 'opposite' or 'on the contrary'. As a linking word, it starts a clause that says the opposite of what you might expect. As an adjective, it describes two opposite things: 跟…相反 'the opposite of…'.

examples.zh: 他 没 生气 ， 相反 ， 还 笑 了 。

grammar.title: 顺便 'while you're at it'
grammar.pattern: Main action，顺便 + extra action
grammar.explain: 顺便 means 'while you're at it' or 'on the way'. It describes doing a small extra thing at the same time as a main action, with little extra effort. It goes before the second verb.

reading.title: 我的朋友小美
reading.zh: 我的好朋友小美是一名护士。她工作很辛苦，常常晚上也要上班，可是她对病人一直很有耐心。有一次，一位老人身体难受，脾气很不好，还批评了她几句。小美一点儿也没生气，相反，她每天都去陪老人聊天。后来，老人离开医院的时候特别感谢她。今年，医院给小美发了奖金。我打电话祝贺她，她开玩笑说：“这些钱正好够请你吃一顿饭。”我们约好周末见面。吃饭的时候，她提醒我少吃盐，少喝甜饮料，例如果汁和奶茶。她说：“你每天都喝那么多饮料，身体会受不了的。”我觉得她的主意很对，决定改一改自己的习惯。吃完饭，我们去公园散步，顺便参观了公园里的植物园。我们认识十年了，偶尔也会吵架，但是我们的友谊一直很好。
reading.en: My good friend Xiao Mei is a nurse. Her work is hard and she often has to work at night, but she has always been very patient with her patients. Once an elderly man felt unwell and was in a very bad mood; he even told her off a few times. Xiao Mei didn't get angry at all. On the contrary, she went to chat with him every day. Later, when he left the hospital, he thanked her warmly. This year the hospital gave Xiao Mei a bonus. I called to congratulate her, and she joked, 'This money is just enough to treat you to a meal.' We agreed to meet at the weekend. Over dinner she reminded me to eat less salt and drink fewer sweet drinks, such as juice and milk tea. She said, 'You drink so many of these drinks every day — your body won't be able to take it.' I thought her advice was right and decided to change my habits. After dinner we went for a walk in the park and visited the botanical garden there while we were at it. We've known each other for ten years, and although we occasionally argue, our friendship has always been strong.

reading.title: 我们的新家
reading.zh: 上个月，我和妻子搬进了新家。新家在城市的东边，对面就是一个公园，窗户外面有几棵大树，风景很美。为了选这个地方，我们商量了很久。首先，这里交通方便，离地铁站只有几分钟；其次，价格也比较合适。搬家那天，天气特别热，我们一边搬东西一边出汗。搬完以后，我们去买家具。妻子的特点是买东西很认真，往往要看好几家店才决定。我的脾气比较急，可是这次我很有耐心，陪她逛了一整天。最后我们用信用卡买了一个沙发和一个大书架。现在，每天晚上我们坐在沙发上阅读，或者稍微看一会儿电视。虽然我们不是很富，但是我觉得我们一点儿也不穷，因为我们有一个温暖的家。
reading.en: Last month my wife and I moved into our new home. It's on the east side of the city, right opposite a park, and there are several big trees outside the window, so the view is lovely. We talked for a long time before choosing this place. First, the transport is convenient — it's only a few minutes from the subway station. Second, the price was quite reasonable. On moving day it was extremely hot, and we were sweating as we carried things in. Afterwards we went to buy furniture. My wife's way of shopping is to be very thorough; she usually looks at several shops before making a decision. I'm rather impatient by nature, but this time I was very patient and spent the whole day shopping with her. In the end we bought a sofa and a big bookcase with a credit card. Now every evening we sit on the sofa and read, or watch a little TV. Although we aren't rich, I don't feel poor at all, because we have a warm home.

grammar.title: 来/去 + purpose

grammar.explain: 来 or 去 can link a movement to its purpose: 去动物园看老虎 'go to the zoo to see the tigers'. 来 can also link a method to a purpose: 用写日记来练习汉语 'practice Chinese by keeping a diary'. The purpose always comes after 来/去.

grammar.title: 再…也… 'no matter how…'

grammar.explain: 再 + adjective or verb, followed by 也 in the next clause, means 'no matter how…, still…'. It stresses that even in an extreme case the result stays the same. The second clause is often negative or expresses determination.

reading.title: 五月十日 星期六 晴
reading.zh: 今天学校组织我们去动物园。早上七点半，大家在学校门口集合，然后乘坐公共汽车出发。到了动物园，我们先去看老虎。老虎正躺在地上睡觉，看起来极其安静。接着我们去看猴子，它们跑来跑去，一会儿上树，一会儿下来，大家都笑了。忽然，一只小猴子拿走了小明的帽子，小明急得大叫。旁边一位师傅马上过来帮忙，最后帽子拿回来了，可是已经脏了。中午，我们坐在草地上吃东西，王老师给我们讲了很多关于动物的知识，她说话非常幽默。下午回学校以前，老师让我们总结今天学到的东西。我觉得每种动物都有自己的优点。回家以后，我马上写了这篇日记。
reading.en: Today the school took us to the zoo. At half past seven in the morning we all gathered at the school gate, then set off by bus. When we got to the zoo, we went to see the tigers first. The tigers were lying on the ground asleep and looked extremely calm. Next we went to see the monkeys. They were running all over the place, climbing up trees one moment and coming down the next, and we all laughed. Suddenly a little monkey grabbed Xiao Ming's hat, and Xiao Ming shouted in panic. A keeper nearby came over at once to help. In the end the hat was returned, but it was already dirty. At noon we sat on the grass and ate, and Ms Wang told us lots of facts about animals; she's really funny. Before we went back to school in the afternoon, the teacher asked us to sum up what we had learned. I think every animal has its own strengths. As soon as I got home, I wrote this diary entry.

reading.title: 一次出差
reading.zh: 上个星期，经理通知我去上海出差三天。因为时间很少，我当天晚上就开始收拾东西：几件衬衫、几双袜子、一条毛巾，还有一盒饼干。第二天早上，我差点儿来不及去机场，还好航班推迟了半个小时。到了上海，我准时到了那家公司。见面的时候，大家互相握手，他们的经理很有礼貌，还给我们准备了热茶。开会的时候，我按照顺序介绍了我们的计划，大家听完都鼓掌了。我心里有点儿得意。没想到，晚上我开始咳嗽，可能是因为上海的气候比北京湿润，我不太习惯。第二天我去看了大夫，大夫让我多喝水、多休息。虽然这次出差很辛苦，还加了两天班，但是结果很好，我觉得很值得。
reading.en: Last week my manager told me to go to Shanghai on a three-day business trip. As there wasn't much time, I started packing that same evening: a few shirts, several pairs of socks, a towel and a box of biscuits. The next morning I almost didn't make it to the airport in time, but luckily the flight was delayed by half an hour. When I got to Shanghai, I arrived at the company right on time. When we met, everyone shook hands. Their manager was very polite and had even prepared hot tea for us. In the meeting I presented our plan point by point, and when I finished, everyone applauded. I felt rather pleased with myself. Unexpectedly, I started coughing that evening, maybe because Shanghai's climate is more humid than Beijing's and I wasn't used to it. The next day I went to see a doctor, who told me to drink plenty of water and get lots of rest. Although the trip was tiring and I worked overtime for two days, the result was good, and I think it was well worth it.

grammar.title: …之一 'one of…'
grammar.pattern: A + 是 + (最 + Adjective + 的) + Noun + 之一
grammar.explain: A 是…之一 means 'A is one of…'. The group is often described with 最 + adjective: 最有名的地方之一 'one of the most famous places'. 之 is a literary form of 的, so 之一 literally means 'one of them'.

grammar.title: Verb + 出来 'out (produced or identified)'

grammar.explain: 出来 after a verb can mean physically 'out', but it often shows that something is produced or recognized: 打印出来 'print out', 写出来 'write out', 看出来 'tell (by looking)', 听出来 'recognize (by sound)'. Add 得 or 不 for 'can' or 'can't': 看不出来 'can't tell'.

reading.title: 我想当导游
reading.zh: 大学毕业以后，我一直想当一名导游。上个月，我在网上看到一家旅游公司正在招聘导游，就马上报了名。我先认真地写好了表格，又把材料打印出来，寄给了他们。一个星期以后，公司通知我去面试。面试那天，路上堵车堵得很厉害，我差点儿迟到。经理问我：“你为什么想做导游？”我说：“我从小在农村长大，喜欢跟不同的人交流。我会说好几种语言，还去过十几次长城，可以给客人介绍它的历史。”经理听了很满意，还表扬我的回答很有意思。不过他也提醒我，导游工作很辛苦，节日的时候也很少能请假。我说我愿意先积累经验，以后也许自己做生意。第二天，公司打电话告诉我：我通过了！
reading.en: Ever since graduating from university, I've wanted to be a tour guide. Last month I saw online that a travel company was hiring guides, so I applied right away. First I carefully filled in the form, then printed out my documents and sent them off. A week later, the company asked me to come for an interview. On the day, the traffic was terrible and I was nearly late. The manager asked me, 'Why do you want to be a tour guide?' I said, 'I grew up in the countryside, and I like communicating with different people. I speak several languages, and I've been to the Great Wall more than ten times, so I can tell visitors about its history.' The manager was very satisfied and even praised my answer for being interesting. But he also reminded me that a guide's work is hard and that it's rarely possible to take time off during holidays. I said I was willing to build up experience first, and perhaps start my own business later. The next day, the company called to tell me I'd got the job!

grammar.title: Fractions and percentages with 分之
grammar.pattern: Denominator + 分之 + Numerator；百分之 + Number
grammar.explain: Chinese fractions say the whole first: 三分之一 is 'one third' (literally 'of three parts, one'). Percentages use 百分之: 百分之二十 is 'twenty percent'. 分之 always sits between the two numbers.

grammar.title: 除了…以外 'besides; except'
grammar.pattern: 除了 A (以外)，Subject + 还/也 + B；除了 A (以外)，Subject + 都 + …
grammar.explain: 除了…以外 means 'besides' or 'except'. With 还 or 也 in the second clause, A is included: 'besides A, also B'. With 都 (or a negative), A is left out: 'everyone except A'. 以外 can be dropped.

reading.title: 我的留学生活
reading.zh: 去年九月，我来到中国留学。出发以前，我去大使馆申请了签证，还换了一些人民币。刚开始，我的汉语不太流利，上课的时候常常听不懂，只好每天晚上认真预习，遇到不认识的词就查词典。老师说我写汉字的时候有点儿马虎，填空题常常因为粗心写错。在老师的帮助下，我养成了每天写日记的习惯，现在已经能用汉语写出几百字的文章了。我们班一共有二十一个学生，其中三分之一是亚洲人，其他的同学是从别的国家来的。寒假的时候，中国朋友请我去他家过年。我们一起包饺子，一起说“干杯”，还看了电视上的京剧表演。放暑假以后，我打算去看看长江，感受一下南方湿润的气候。
reading.en: Last September I came to China to study. Before I left, I went to the embassy to apply for a visa and changed some money into renminbi. At first my Chinese wasn't very fluent and I often couldn't understand what was said in class, so I had to prepare carefully every evening and look up words I didn't know in the dictionary. My teacher said I was a bit sloppy when writing characters and often made careless mistakes in fill-in-the-blank questions. With my teacher's help, I got into the habit of keeping a diary every day, and now I can already write articles of several hundred characters in Chinese. There are twenty-one students in our class; a third of them are Asian, and the others come from other countries. During the winter vacation, a Chinese friend invited me to his home for the New Year. We made dumplings together, said 'Cheers!' together and watched Beijing opera on TV. When the summer holidays start, I plan to go and see the Yangtze River and experience the humid southern climate.
